 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Houston Texans are facing a critical Thursday Night Football matchup in NFL Week 11 with their playoff hopes hanging in the balance. Houston cannot afford many more setbacks as the season enters a pivotal stretch, but the team will be forced to navigate its Week 11 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts without several key contributors.
 The Texans have already dealt with injuries throughout the season, and the latest developments leave both sides of the football dealing with significant absences ahead of kickoff.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Predicting upsets in Week 11 of NFL season 
 Texans lose Woody Marks, Marvin Harrison Jr. and Danielle Hunter 
 Oct 25, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans running back Woody Marks (4) runs with the ball during the third quarter against the New York Giants at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
 Houston will be without running back Woody Marks, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive end Danielle Hunter for Thursday night's matchup against the Colts.
 Marks was ruled out after suffering a concussion during Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns. The running back had been an important part of Houston's rushing attack, making his absence a significant setback heading into a game the Texans desperately need to win.
 Harrison Jr. is also unavailable after dealing with a hamstring injury, while Hunter will miss another game with a hamstring injury of his own. Hunter's absence is particularly significant for a Houston defense that needs to find ways to disrupt opposing offenses and generate pressure.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Losing three key players on a short week leaves Houston with little time to adjust its game plan before facing Indianapolis.
 MORE: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 11 
 Houston faces enormous pressure against the Colts 
 The Texans enter Thursday night's matchup needing to get back on track after a disappointing loss to Cleveland. Houston had an opportunity to secure a much-needed victory but ultimately let the game slip away, making the Colts matchup even more important.
 With Marks unavailable, Houston will need to adjust its backfield plans. Fortunately, David Montgomery is expected to return after missing four consecutive games with a groin injury, giving the Texans another option at running back. Montgomery was listed without an injury designation after participating fully in practice throughout the week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, his return does little to offset the overall impact of the Texans' injury situation. Losing Hunter on the defensive side and Harrison Jr. on offense further limits Houston's options in a game with major implications for its season.
 The Texans need a win Thursday night to keep their playoff hopes alive, but they'll have to overcome significant personnel losses to get it done. With several key players unavailable, the pressure is firmly on the remaining healthy players to deliver when Houston needs them most.
